question: Should aggregate token-and-cost reporting become an extension of `openclaw gateway usage-cost` / `openclaw status --usage`, or is a separate top-level `openclaw stats` API an intended long-term CLI surface?
rationale: Both the existing documented commands and the proposed command report overlapping usage information, so implementation quality alone cannot choose the public CLI boundary.

options.title: Extend the existing usage command
options.body: Move any missing multi-agent, filtering, JSON, or breakdown capability into the established usage-reporting surface and avoid a parallel top-level command.

options.title: Sponsor a distinct stats API
options.body: Keep `openclaw stats` only with an explicit durable contract that distinguishes it from provider quota/status and gateway session-cost reporting.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Close or pause the branch until maintainers decide whether aggregate session accounting deserves a separate public CLI namespace.

recommendation.title: Extend the existing usage command
recommendation.body: Move any missing multi-agent, filtering, JSON, or breakdown capability into the established usage-reporting surface and avoid a parallel top-level command.

likelyOwner.reason: The current docs route users to the existing CLI usage surfaces, making this person the strongest available routing candidate for the command-boundary decision.
